title: TNTComplEx relation x time Mirror factor bank
hypothesis: On a synthetic temporal graph whose relation-time operators are generated by a shared low-dimensional periodic basis, a shared physical time-relation basis plus compact Mirror coordinates can recover future relation-time links with fewer serialized bytes than native TNTComplEx temporal factors and a byte-near Tucker/low-rank control, while retaining chronological generalization; on independently sampled relation-time operators it should need private residual state.
mirror_coordinate: per relation compact coefficients selecting a periodic time-view combination
controls: native periodic temporal relation modulation with fixed shared time features
TuckER-style relation coefficient x fixed time feature x shared operator basis
independent relation-time operators (diagnostic only; not a valid unseen-future upper control because future timestamp rows are untrained)
task: binary temporal link ranking on generated entity-relation-time triples; report filtered MRR and Hits@1

development.selection_metric: development filtered MRR with serialized payload bytes; choose only rank and Mirror coefficient budget

fresh.split: chronological training times 0..7, development 8..9, fresh audit 10..11; audit relation-time pairs are held out, and all training triples precede audit timestamps

success_gate: On at least 2/3 fresh aligned worlds, Mirror filtered MRR >= 0.95 * native periodic temporal baseline and >= 0.95 * byte-near Tucker/low-rank control while actual payload <= 0.60 * native TNTComplEx-style periodic baseline; report independent-operator boundary and compute. This supports only an aligned synthetic mechanism result.
failure_gate: Observed: Mirror and equally sized TuckER have identical aligned-world MRR on all 3 seeds (same function family and matched state), so no Mirror-specific gain; serialized Mirror payload is >60% native payload. The preregistered storage gate is not met. Independent operators are not a valid future-time upper control because their future timestamp rows receive no training; report as unavailable/diagnostic only.
boundaries: synthetic graph only; no benchmark reproduction
fixed-update learning efficiency is not capacity evidence
logical relation-time combinations do not imply independent capacity
amendment_1: Before fresh audit: correct time extrapolation validity. All methods now receive the same fixed 8-period sinusoidal timestamp features; train timestamps 0..7 and evaluate unseen future timestamps 8..11. This prevents an embedding-only failure from deciding the temporal generalization question. Amendment based only on development diagnostics; audit seeds remain unopened.
amendment_2: After initial audit run and before result interpretation, noticed audit script aggregated timestamps 8..11 although preregistered fresh window is 10..11. No model or hyperparameter choices were made from these values. Reran the exact fixed models/seeds/updates with evaluation restricted to 10..11; initial aggregate is retained as source/initial_audit_deviation.json for provenance.
amendment_3: Corrected the metric implementation to filtered MRR by removing the other known positive tail for the same (head, relation, timestamp) from each candidate ranking. This metric bug was found during protocol audit before interpreting final results. Reran the exact fixed fresh seeds and training configuration; earlier runs remain archived.
amendment_4: Removed non-forward unused relation parameters discovered by final payload audit. These tensors were not read by any scoring path but were present in earlier serialized states. Final audit payloads now include only forward-reachable learned tensors and deterministic time features. Same fresh seeds and update schedule rerun; prior files retained.
